key_insight: VesNet uses a neural network to accelerate the most expensive vesicle self-interaction calculations in Stokes flow while preserving the physics of the full suspension solver.
engineering_relevance: This hybrid approach enables fast, GPU-accelerated simulation of large vesicle suspensions, making high-fidelity deformable-particle modeling more practical for research and engineering workflows.
method: Approximates vesicle self-interactions, including background-flow coupling and short-range lubrication forces, with a neural network.
Keeps conventional boundary reparameterization and far-field hydrodynamics modules in the solver.
Runs on GPU for major speedups over CPU and GPU boundary-integral baselines.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports over 100x speedup versus a multithreaded MATLAB CPU boundary-integral solver and about 5x versus its GPU counterpart, while reproducing single-vesicle, pair, and large-suspension dynamics.
watch_item: Accuracy and robustness may depend on how well the neural approximation generalizes across flow conditions, vesicle shapes, and near-contact lubrication regimes.
paper_title: VesNet: Neural network accelerated solver for simulating Stokesian vesicle suspensions
